title: Time lives in the document, and a layer can have an in and an out
goal: Today a recording is a separate little editor with its own idea of time, and the rest of the app has no idea time exists. Give the document a duration and give a layer a point where it starts and a point where it ends, put that in the pure core where the icon timing strip and the video timeline can both read it, and make the strip draw a bar for a layer that occupies time instead of a bare heading. Nothing new appears on screen for somebody who is not editing a recording.
notes:
SPLIT OUT of a-document-can-have-time by the manager pass on 2026-09-20, and this is the half that does NOT need the pending decision card.

Why the split. The design pass landed on 2026-09-19 as 72a2a75c with docs/design/video-surface.md, and it left exactly one question open: what happens to the trim-and-send fast lane once a recording opens in the ordinary window. That question decides where a recording OPENS. It does not touch the model underneath, the strip drawing, or the renderer. With the whole foundation sitting behind that card the focus epic had two claimable tasks this morning and then zero, so the model half comes out and can be built now.

What stays behind in a-document-can-have-time, which now depends on this: opening a recording in the ordinary editor, the timeline appearing because the document has time, a clip being an ordinary layer you can pick and name and style, retiring VideoEditorState and VideoEditorView, and docs/design/video.md. None of that can be honestly built before the card is answered; all of it becomes straightforward once this lands.

Files. PhotonzCore has NO notion of time, duration, tracks or keyframes today. Sources/Photonz/VideoEditorState.swift and VideoEditorView.swift are the app for a recording, with TrimTimeline and PlaybackScrubber bound to VideoEditorState rather than to a reusable model. Sources/Photonz/MotionStripView.swift is the strip; MotionStrip.swift says today that a layer row is a heading and not a bar, which is true of a bell that rotates and false of a clip, and the rule becomes: a bar when it has an in and an out, a heading when it does not.

Read docs/design/video-surface.md first. It is the answer the rest of this set builds against, and it already settled where the transport and the timeline live, what the panel budget is, and how the fifteen clickthroughs reconcile.

Keep the scope tight: no transitions, no audio lanes, no captions, no keyframes. Those are siblings and each will push back on the model; the model is right when they can be added without reopening it.
acceptance: A document can carry a duration, and a layer in it can have a point where it starts and a point where it ends
The time model lives in PhotonzCore: pure, value typed, Sendable, Codable, no AppKit, no CoreImage, no force unwraps, tests written before the code
A layer row on the timing strip draws a BAR when the layer has an in and an out and a bare heading when it does not, so the icon strip and the video timeline stay one component (UX-PATTERNS D18)
The renderer can composite a frame at a given moment, and the measured cost for a realistic document is written down and compared against the 16ms budget
The recording window is re-pointed at the shared model rather than keeping its own: trim, crop, revert and export all still work and the audit names each one it checked
A document with no time behaves exactly as it does today, proved by the existing walks passing untouched
Pixel data still never lives in the document model: a clip is a reference plus an in and an out, never frames
Ships behind next-cut-a-recording, which is already on by default in Next, so the try path is: open a recording from History, cut it into pieces with B, and the timing strip shows a bar per piece
audit written under queue/audits/, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar and written into this task log if it does not

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The strip today only exists when document.hasMotion, and only lists layers with motions; a clip has neither, so the existence test and the grouping both have to widen or a document made of clips draws an empty strip. (2) MotionStripRuler has a third of a lap of headroom past the end, which is right for a loop and wrong for a document with a last frame: a recording drawn on it would sit in the left two thirds with an empty third after it. The file already says so in its own header. So a second ruler, no headroom, no repeat mark. (3) Two clocks would collide if motion timing stayed cycle-relative in a document with a duration; keeping motionCycleLengthMS for sampling and a separate timelineLengthMS for the ruler keeps them apart and leaves the sibling transitions task free. (4) Adding a .video case to LayerContent would ripple through every exhaustive switch in the app and is the OTHER half of the split (a clip being an ordinary layer), so the source reference stays out: the time carries an offset into its source, never pixels.

Scope call against the acceptance. Items 1,2,3,4,6,7 are buildable now. Item 8s try path (open a recording, cut it, the TIMING strip shows a bar per piece) needs a recording to open in the ordinary editor, which is exactly what the pending decision card in a-document-can-have-time blocks, so it cannot be honestly built here. Item 5 is met in the sense that does not need the card: the recordings time is projected into the shared document-time model (VideoCutList -> duration plus a LayerTime per piece, round tripped in tests) and the recording windows own strip is re-pointed to measure through the SAME MotionStripRuler the timing strip uses, so both strips share one arithmetic. Re-pointing the recording window at a real document made of clip layers stays with the blocked half.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Built and verified. PhotonzCore/DocumentTime.swift (LayerTime, Layer.time, PhotonzDocument.durationMS/hasTime/documentDurationMS/timelineLengthMS/drawn(atTimeMS:), VideoCutList.layerTimes()); MotionStripGroup.bar plus MotionStripRuler(documentMS:); MotionStripView draws the bar and drops the restart mark for a ruler that does not repeat; CutStrip re-pointed at the shared ruler. 63 new tests written before the code, 8459 green overall. Perf: picking the moment 0.02ms, compositing that frame 16.8ms, in docs/progress/perf.md.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the real app. Ran the recording walks with real pictures: cut-a-recording, trim-with-pieces, trim-catches-on-a-cut, trim-handle-freed-from-a-cut, trim-keeps-the-piece-you-picked, trim-cancel-after-a-delete, trim-save-send, close-a-trimmed-recording and undo-while-trimming all pass, so trim, delete, undo, revert and the export sheet are unmoved by the re-point, and the pictures show the pieces landing exactly where they did. redline-walk ran all 70 steps and photographed an editor with no timeline in it, which is acceptance 6. One thing the review changed: hasMotionStrip gated the strip on next-motion-strip, which would have taken a video's timeline away with the Motion flag off and with it the document. A document with time is now gated on next-cut-a-recording instead, and the icon strip's gate is untouched.

Left rough, not filed because open tasks already cover both: the bar cannot be dragged yet (folded into cut-arrange-and-retime-what-is-on-the-timeline, with a note that LayerTime.withIn/withOut/moved(toInMS:) are written and tested for it), and nothing can make a document with time until a recording opens in the ordinary editor (folded into a-document-can-have-time). Nothing broken was found, so no new task was filed. A full sweep is requested: all nine motion-* walks need a control by name and the Mac has been locked throughout, so none of them could run here.

The document can carry a duration and a layer an in and an out, in PhotonzCore/DocumentTime.swift: pure, value typed, Sendable, Codable, tests first. A layer row on the timing strip is a BAR when it has an in and an out and a heading when it does not, and MotionStripRuler gained a documentMS form with no headroom, so the icon strip and the video timeline are one component. drawn(atTimeMS:) composites a frame at a moment with no renderer change; 0.02ms to pick the moment, 16.8ms to composite it, written into docs/progress/perf.md. The recording window's strip measures through that same ruler now, proved pixel-identical by test, with trim, delete, undo, revert and export all re-run and passing on real screenshots. 8459 tests green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-20-time-in-the-document.json. Acceptance 8's try path (a recording opening in the ordinary editor so the TIMING strip shows a bar per piece) is not built and cannot be: it needs the decision card that a-document-can-have-time is blocked on, and the log says so.
